hook.text: A journalist sends Almaty Air Initiative five questions. Answering takes hours: three pages, twenty-three sources.

title.text: Taza Copilot answers in seconds, in English, Russian or Kazakh.

answer.text: Every answer comes from a hundred and four AAI sources, with the exact quote, the page, and a link.

differ.text: When sources disagree, it shows both. And it checks any claim from the news.

live.text: Live data from a hundred and fifty sensors: the map, the best time to go out, and comparisons with other cities.

schools.text: Schools ranked by the air right now. A policy brief, a quote card or a citation from any answer.

accuracy.text: Accuracy is measured: forty-four out of forty-four, including real questions journalists sent AAI.

admin.text: The AAI team uploads a new report, and Taza quotes it seconds later.

voice.text: Talk to it: the voice agent answers and drives the page. A guided tour explains the rest.

channels.text: It is everywhere: Telegram alerts, WhatsApp chat and calls, a website widget, and a phone app.

trust.text: History stays in your browser, any AI model works, keys stay on the server, and it costs about seven dollars a month.

driver.text: Drivers get a morning push on bad-air days, and a reminder to close the windows in traffic jams.

rider.text: Riders see the air at their pickup point. Drivers find a cleaner spot for a break.

api.text: All from one API call, with no personal data.

outro.text: Answers in seconds instead of hours. Ready for Almaty today, and Kathmandu and Lahore next.
